encounters.cc: Agitation and confusion developing during management of hypertensive emergency

lines: Agitation and confusion developing during management of hypertensive emergency

This 73-year-old male with heart failure with reduced ejection fraction, stage 3 CKD, and history of hyperkalemia and nephritis is admitted to the intensive care unit for management of a hypertensive emergency.
He is started on an intravenous infusion of nitroprusside.
After 72 hours of treatment, the nursing staff reports that the patient has become increasingly agitated and confused.
- Heart failure with reduced ejection fraction
- Father: Hypertension, Paget disease of bone
Smoking: Never smoker. Alcohol: None. Occupation: Retired.
His blood pressure is now 130/85 mmHg.
His respiratory rate is 22 breaths per minute, and oxygen saturation is 96% on room air.
On examination, the patient is disoriented to time and place, and his speech is slurred.
He has no focal neurological deficits.
